reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossed design over who supplies the instruction slot (bare / hand-written spec / GEPA / MIPRO) against what is injected (real, content-substituted, order-shuffled, cross-query, skeleton, fixed, padding), claiming that retrieved agent memory helps only by supplying a syntax + procedural-schema scaffold that any instruction stating that scaffold already supplies, leaving memory with a net-negative content residual.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, and together they take most of the novelty. (1) GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025) — cited here only as an optimizer, but its headline empirical claim is precisely that reflectively evolved natural-language instructions outperform few-shot demonstration search (MIPROv2 with bootstrapped demos), i.e. that the instruction slot substitutes for the demonstration slot. P2/P5 is that finding re-run with retrieved memory rather than bootstrapped demos in the demonstration slot; the proposal never engages with it as a novelty threat, which a reviewer will notice immediately since GEPA is the optimizer being used. (2) Boshi Wang et al., 'Towards Understanding Chain-of-Thought Prompting: An Empirical Study of What Matters' (ACL 2023), and Madaan & Yazdanbakhsh, 'Text and Patterns' (2022), which already decompose demonstrations into bridging objects (content) versus language templates/patterns (schema+syntax), already permute and corrupt reasoning steps, and already report that relevance and coherence-of-order carry a specific, separable share. E1/E7 is that decomposition transplanted from CoT demos to ReAct trajectories. The proposal's defence — that in agents a malformed output is episode-fatal rather than costing one token — is a real but incremental difference, and E2's parse-failure instrumentation is the only place it is cashed out. Min et al. (2022) is correctly named but is the weaker of the threats. What remains genuinely unclaimed is narrow: the specific crossing of memory against a *hand-written* scaffold specification (S_SPEC), and the S_GEPA-M co-adaptation arm.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary claim is not identified by the design. Two problems compound. First, the gate: the track's own pilot reports that the injected bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven, so REAL−NONE at S0 — the denominator of every channel ratio in E1 and the left half of the P2 contrast — is expected to be at or below zero on this very setup. E0 is written to catch that, but its threshold (4 points) sits below its own minimum detectable effect at n=200 paired (~5 points at the stated 12% discordance), so the gate passes or fails largely by noise, and if it fails, P1, P2 and P3 — three of five confirmatory predictions — are unrunnable and the paper collapses to a re-statement of the pilot's already-known harm result. Second, even if the gate passes, P2 does not distinguish substitution from headroom. S_GEPA+NONE and S_SPEC+NONE are by construction the highest-accuracy memory-free cells; a fixed-size benefit added on top of a higher baseline shrinks in accuracy points under any monotone ceiling, with no scaffold-substitution mechanism whatever. The proposal half-notices this by fitting a mixed-effects logistic model, but then states P2's decision rule in raw points ('≥5 points at S0 to ≤2 points at S_GEPA'): the pre-registered test is on the log-odds scale and the pre-registered prediction is on the probability scale, and these can disagree in both directions, so the confirmatory rule is ambiguous before a single episode is run. Third, and separately fatal for the harm family: E3/P4 conditions on items correct under NONE and then compares break counts across conditions. That conditioning induces regression to the mean, and any condition with lower overall accuracy mechanically breaks more previously-correct items — so 'REAL and CROSS each break ≥2× SCRAMBLE-C at S_GEPA' is substantially entailed by the accuracy ordering the same experiment is trying to explain, not by content.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add an accuracy-matched, scaffold-free instruction level — call it S_CONTENT: a hand-written instruction of the same length as S_SPEC that raises accuracy through task framing, hints or encouragement while stating nothing about output grammar, step budget, action ordering or stopping. If REAL's gain collapses at S_SPEC/S_GEPA but survives at an accuracy-matched S_CONTENT, substitution is about the scaffold; if it collapses at both, the whole result is headroom and the paper has no mechanism. Without this arm P2 is uninterpretable. (2) Pick one scale and one estimand for P2 before running: a logit-scale interaction as primary with a points-scale contrast declared secondary (or vice versa), not one as the test and the other as the threshold. (3) Add an oracle-memory arm and report the content channel relative to it. (4) Re-do the harm analysis as a paired model over all 700 items (e.g. condition × baseline-outcome interaction, or a paired comparison of REAL-vs-SCRAMBLE-C discordance directly, which is legitimate) instead of conditioning on the NONE-correct subset. (5) Pre-specify what SCRAMBLE-C's substituted observations do: entity-swapped observations are, by construction, factually false relative to the live Wikipedia index, so SCRAMBLE-C may be teaching observation fabrication rather than 'pure scaffold'; the 10% hand-screen checks fidelity of the rewrite, not whether the rewritten trajectory is now a hallucination demonstration. Add a fabrication-rate metric on the agent's own observations as a mechanism check. (6) Run the collision search — even manually, even reading only GEPA's and MIPRO's own instruction-versus-demonstration ablations — before submission.
reviews.missing_baseline: An oracle / upper-bound memory arm: inject the gold trajectory for the evaluated query itself (or the trajectory of a near-duplicate training query) at S0 and at S_GEPA. Every content-channel estimate in the plan (P3's ≤30% claim, the REAL−CROSS estimand, the whole 'memory earns its tokens only on idiosyncratic content' conclusion) is otherwise unidentifiable from simple retriever failure: bge-base top-4 over a 500-episode bank on HotpotQA distractor may just be retrieving nothing useful, in which case 'content contributes little' is a fact about this bank, not about content. A reviewer will demand the ceiling before accepting a null. Two further omissions worth naming: MIPRO is deliberately run in instruction-only mode with demonstration bootstrapping disabled, which removes the actual deployed competitor — full MIPRO with bootstrapped demos is the system whose demo slot memory is supposed to be replacing — and there is no accuracy-matched scaffold-free instruction level (see above).
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin, it is empty: it reports that every search call failed, for the second consecutive revision, and the author states plainly that novelty is unverified. The honesty is creditable, and the retraction of the fabricated 'ExpRAG (arXiv:2603.18272)' identifier is exactly right and should be read in the proposal's favour on integrity. But under the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness, this is a substantial deduction, not a neutral: no closest-prior-work determination has been made, and the two threats I can name from background knowledge — GEPA's own instruction-versus-few-shot-demonstration result, and the CoT template-versus-bridging-object ablation line (Boshi Wang et al. ACL 2023; Madaan & Yazdanbakhsh 2022) — are both findable without any search tool at all, from papers the proposal already cites or uses. That they are absent from the Related Work's threat analysis suggests the gap is not only tooling. I cannot verify a specific 2025-2026 arXiv preprint that runs the crossed format/content decomposition on agent trajectories, and I will not invent one; but the 2025 agent-memory line (ReasoningBank and successors) is moving fast toward negative-transfer and memory-harm ablations, and the declared fallback — 're-position around E5/E7' — is weak, because E7 (step-order permutation) is the arm closest to Wang et al.'s existing perturbation study and E5's substitution framing is closest to GEPA's own thesis. The fallback ground may already be occupied.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossed ablation arguing that retrieved agent memory helps mainly by supplying a scaffold — split into a surface tool-call-syntax channel and a procedural-schema channel — so that any adequate instruction (hand-written S_SPEC, GEPA, or MIPRO) substitutes for it, leaving memory's residual content channel as a net-negative contributor.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Min et al. (EMNLP 2022) is the acknowledged conceptual ancestor and the proposal handles it honestly, but it is not the sharpest threat. Synapse (Zheng et al., ICLR 2024) already abstracts retrieved trajectories by stripping task-specific state while preserving structure, and Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024) already induces reusable procedural workflows rather than storing episode content — both are, in effect, arguments that the reusable part of experience is schema rather than content, which directly contradicts the Related Work claim that 'nobody removes content while holding format fixed.' The second threat is GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025) itself, whose headline is that reflectively evolved instructions outperform demonstration-based prompt optimization; if that comparison already exists in print, P2 ('the optimizer's instruction slot substitutes for the demonstration slot') is a restatement, and only the syntax/schema split (E7) and the harm attribution (E3/P4) remain unclaimed. The MIPRO/DSPy component ablations on instructions-vs-bootstrapped-demos are a third, weaker version of the same collision.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory core is conditioned on a gain the authors' own pilot says does not exist, and the arithmetic that would interpret it is not a decomposition. (1) Gate E0 requires REAL to beat NONE at S0 by >=4 points, yet the track's motivating pilot reports that injected memory fixed zero items and broke six to seven; the expected denominator (REAL - NONE at S0) is therefore <=0, and P1, P2 and P3 all divide by it. Worse, E0 is run at n=200 while the paper's own power model (2.8 points at n=700, 12% discordance) implies an MDE near 5.2 points at n=200 — the gate threshold sits below what the gate can measure, so a study-defining branch is decided by noise. The declared fallback (harm-side results only) is precisely the pilot's already-published finding. (2) Even if the gate passes, the three 'channels' do not partition the gain: syntax (SCRAMBLE-C-SHUF - NONE) + schema (SCRAMBLE-C - SHUF) + content (REAL - CROSS) equals (REAL - NONE) only if acc(SCRAMBLE-C) = acc(CROSS), which nothing enforces and no arm checks. P1 (>=60%) and P3 (<=30%) can both be met with a large unaccounted or double-counted residual, and no coherence constraint is pre-registered. (3) P2's interaction is confounded with baseline level: S_GEPA raises accuracy, so a smaller REAL increment on top of it is the expected diminishing-return/ceiling pattern, not evidence of scaffold substitution — and the pre-registered threshold ('>=5 points falling to <=2 points') is stated in accuracy points while the single primary test is a logistic interaction on log-odds, where the two can license opposite conclusions on the same data. (4) SCRAMBLE-C-SHUF permutes action steps of a ReAct trace, so observations no longer follow the actions that produced them; the 'schema channel' estimate (SCRAMBLE-C minus SHUF) is contaminated by the penalty for an incoherent exemplar and can even go negative, which E7's promotion to confirmatory control does not fix.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes. (a) Add S_VERBOSE: an instruction matched to S_GEPA in token count and register but containing no syntax, schema, step-budget or stopping information, and run the P2 interaction against it. Without this, every S_SPEC/S_GEPA contrast confounds 'the instruction states the scaffold' with 'the instruction is longer'; PAD length-matches the injection slot only, never the instruction slot. (b) Drop the ratio framing unless acc(SCRAMBLE-C) ~ acc(CROSS) is empirically verified: report syntax, schema and content in raw accuracy points with an explicit residual term, and pre-register the primary contrast and its threshold on one scale (log-odds), with the accuracy-point version demoted to secondary. (c) Run the gate at full n=700, or raise the gate threshold to what n=200 can detect; and given the pilot, make the harm-side paper (E3/P4 plus substitution-on-harm) the primary deliverable rather than the fallback, so the contribution does not evaporate on a coin flip. (d) Replace the full permutation in SCRAMBLE-C-SHUF with a coherence-preserving reordering (swap two independent sub-goal blocks) so the schema estimate is not the cost of exemplar incoherence, and restore one affordance-bearing environment (ALFWorld or WebShop) at reduced n — on search-tool multi-hop QA there is almost no experience-idiosyncratic content for memory to carry, so the deflationary result is close to guaranteed and correspondingly uninformative, and E9, the only arm that looks for the boundary, is explicitly underpowered at n~100 per stratum.
reviews.missing_baseline: The optimizer's own demonstration slot. MIPRO is run with demonstration bootstrapping disabled and GEPA with no exemplars, so the plan never evaluates optimizer-selected bootstrapped demonstrations drawn from the 100-item dev slice (call it BOOTSTRAP-DEMO) as an injection condition. That is the cheapest content-bearing competitor to retrieved memory and the composition the field actually deploys; without it the claim 'memory earns its tokens only on experience-idiosyncratic content' is never tested against static optimized demos, and FIXED-REAL does not stand in for it because it involves no selection or optimization. Second omission: the length-matched instruction control S_VERBOSE described above.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin — it is empty, and the authors say so. Zero searches completed across two consecutive revisions, novelty argued entirely from unverified recollection, and the prior version carried a fabricated arXiv identifier (retracted here, to their credit). By the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this alone caps novelty: the proposal has not established that E1 is unclaimed. I cannot name a 2026 preprint from inside this review either, but I can name the checks that must be run before submission and that the authors' own recollection already puts at risk: GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025) on instruction evolution outperforming demonstration-based optimization, which is P2 in different clothing; Synapse and Agent Workflow Memory, which already strip episode content while retaining structure; the MIPRO/DSPy instructions-vs-demonstrations component ablations; and the 2025 ReasoningBank line plus the fast-moving 'context rot / long-context distractor' preprint cluster, which is the most likely home of a paper that already attributes injected-memory harm to topically-plausible distractor content. The stated collision policy (re-position onto E5/E7 if E1 collides) is sensible, but a policy is not a search, and the fallback contribution — the syntax/schema split plus the hand-written-spec substitution — is a thinner paper than the one being reviewed.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossed ablation over who supplies the instruction slot (bare / hand-written spec / GEPA / MIPRO) and what is injected (real, content-substituted, order-shuffled, cross-retrieved, skeleton, padded) that claims retrieved agent memory helps almost entirely through a scaffold decomposable into a syntax channel and a procedural-schema channel, so that any instruction stating the scaffold makes memory's gain collapse while its content-borne harm persists.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Min et al. (EMNLP 2022) is the acknowledged conceptual ancestor and the proposal correctly argues the agent port is not mechanical (episode-fatal malformed actions, an executable action grammar, the added procedural-schema channel). The more dangerous threat is the two optimizers the proposal uses as instruments: MIPRO/DSPy (Opsahl-Ong et al., 2024) reports instruction-only vs demonstration-bearing ablations and characterizes when optimized instructions substitute for bootstrapped demonstrations, and GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025) is argued in its own paper partly on the premise that reflectively evolved instructions can match or beat demonstration-heavy prompts. P2/P5 is close to a restatement of that reported behaviour with a retrieval memory bank in the demonstration slot. The proposal never engages either paper's own instruction-vs-demonstration ablations, so a reviewer will ask what E5/P2 shows that S_GEPA's and S_MIPRO's source papers do not already imply. The genuinely unclaimed piece is narrower than the framing: the SCRAMBLE-C / SCRAMBLE-C-SHUF split (E7) giving separate syntax and procedural-schema point estimates on executable trajectories.
reviews.strongest_objection: P2, the single pre-registered primary test, is confounded with ceiling compression rather than substitution. S_GEPA + NONE is by construction a much stronger baseline than S0 + NONE, and on a bounded exact-match metric an injection's marginal gain shrinks as the baseline rises for reasons that have nothing to do with who supplies a scaffold. Nothing in the 12-cell E1 grid holds memory-free accuracy fixed while varying whether the instruction states the scaffold, so 'REAL's gain falls from >=5 points at S0 to <=2 points at S_GEPA' is exactly what diminishing returns toward a common asymptote produces. The mixed-effects logistic model mitigates this on the logit scale, but every pre-registered threshold (P2, P5, P6, P9) is stated in raw accuracy points, i.e. on the scale where the confound bites. Two aggravating problems ride on top. (1) The <=2-point criterion in P2, P5 and P6 sits below the design's own paired MDE of ~2.8 points, so a confirmatory prediction is 'confirmed' by a difference the study cannot resolve; the substitution result is then indistinguishable from a 2.7-point surviving gain. (2) The entire confirmatory gain family (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6) is conditioned on gate E0 finding REAL beats NONE by >=4 points at S0, yet the track's own motivating pilot found an injected bank that fixed zero items and broke six to seven. The modal outcome is that E0 fails and the paper degrades to E3/P4, which is a re-analysis of the pilot's already-known harm finding. Separately, the channel decomposition is not arithmetically a decomposition: acc(REAL)-acc(NONE) telescopes as [SHUF-NONE] + [C-SHUF] + [REAL-C], but the proposal substitutes REAL-CROSS for the third term. Since CROSS and SCRAMBLE-C are different injections, the three reported 'shares' use incompatible baselines, need not be non-negative, and can sum to well above or below 100%, which makes P1's '>=60%' and P3's '<=30%' thresholds jointly satisfiable by construction rather than by evidence.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Add an accuracy-matched, scaffold-free instruction level: an instruction tuned on the dev slice to lift memory-free accuracy to S_GEPA + NONE's level using task-content directives only, verified by the E5 clause labelling to contain few syntax/schema clauses. If REAL's gain collapses there too, the effect is ceiling compression and the substitution claim is dead; if it survives there and dies at S_SPEC/S_GEPA, the claim is earned. 2) Make the decomposition additive: define the content channel as acc(REAL)-acc(SCRAMBLE-C) so the three channels telescope to the denominator, and keep REAL-CROSS as a separate relevance estimand rather than as 'the content share'. 3) Set every equivalence bound at or above the MDE (>=3 points), or lower the MDE by increasing n or adding a paired continuous secondary metric; a <=2-point criterion at MDE 2.8 should not be pre-registered. 4) Align gate E0 with P2's own antecedent (>=5 points, not >=4) and pre-register the harm-only null paper as the primary deliverable, since the pilot makes that the likely branch. 5) Run at least three GEPA seeds, or drop causal language about optimizers and rest the mechanism on the deterministic S_SPEC level. 6) Use two annotators for P7 who are not authors; an author annotating their own mechanism story inflates kappa on the one diagnostic that could falsify it. 7) Report HotpotQA and HoVer separately: pooling span-extraction exact match with a 2/3-way claim label under one 'exact match' number gives the two subsets different baselines, different chance floors, and different break/fix semantics, and a shift in the mix alone can move every channel ratio. 8) Run the six named searches before submission. 9) Recheck the compute arithmetic: ~28k episodes x ~8 calls x ~2k generated tokens at ~6k-token prompts is on the order of 10^8-10^9 tokens; the claimed ~13 GPU-hours for the 7B evaluation implies an aggregate throughput several times what 4xA100 delivers at that context length, so the '2 days wall-clock' estimate is optimistic by roughly 5-10x even before the optimizer rollouts.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. (a) The accuracy-matched scaffold-free instruction level described above, without which P2's interaction cannot be attributed to scaffold supply rather than to a higher baseline. (b) An oracle-retrieval / gold-relevant memory arm. The whole content-channel result ('memory's content is worth <=30% and is net-negative') is estimated under one retriever (bge-base, k=4) over a bank distilled by a frontier model from 500 episodes. A reviewer will say the paper measured a weak retriever, not a weak channel, and CROSS does not answer this because it lowers relevance rather than raising it. An upper-bound arm that injects the memory item known to contain the needed fact (constructible from the E9 idiosyncratic stratum) is cheap and is the difference between 'content does not help' and 'this retriever does not surface content that helps'. Also notable, though defensibly cut: the mirror of SCRAMBLE-C (content preserved, syntax/schema destroyed) was removed as SCRAMBLE-F, so the format-vs-content claim is only ever probed from the format-preserving side.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is not a thin check, it is an absent one, and by the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral it is the second-largest problem in the submission after the P2 confound. The authors report that every search call failed for the second consecutive revision, and state outright that novelty is unverified against the 2025-2026 literature. Candour is worth something, but a submission cannot discharge its literature search with a list of queries it promises to run later; by submission time the claim either has been checked or has not. Confidence in the unverified background knowledge offered as a substitute is further reduced by the disclosed history of a fabricated citation ('ExpRAG, arXiv:2603.18272') in an earlier version, which is precisely the failure mode that unverified recall produces. I cannot name a specific 2025-2026 preprint that already runs this exact crossed format/content decomposition on executable agent trajectories, and I would not invent one, but the space is dense and moving fast: agent-memory ablation papers in the ReasoningBank/AWM line, and the instruction-versus-demonstration ablations inside the MIPRO and GEPA papers themselves, are all live collision candidates, and the proposal's own collision policy concedes that a crossed decomposition on agent trajectories would supersede E1 and force a retreat to E5/E7. Given that the fallback position (the syntax/schema split and the hand-written-instruction substitution test) is also the only part I judge clearly unclaimed, the proposal is effectively asking reviewers to accept its narrower contribution on trust.
